title: 229. why you’re struggling in college (& what to do) feat. dr. jessi gold
description_html:
oday’s guest is ⁠dr. jessi gold⁠— a nationally recognized psychiatrist, writer, and speaker specializing in mental health care for students, faculty, healthcare professionals, and others in high-stress professions. she is the inaugural chief wellness officer for the university of tennessee system and an associate professor of psychiatry at the university of tennessee health science center.

in this episode, we break down what you need to know about managing your mental health as a college student. this episode has tons of information about the gen z college experience, including why your mental health might struggle in college and how you can ask for help if your mental health is suffering.

summary: sadie and dr. jessi gold, chief wellness officer for the university of tennessee system, talk about why college students struggle with their mental health and how to ask for help. they cover why students don't reach out (comparing themselves to others, feeling not sick enough, not recognizing their own symptoms), what's actually happening on campuses (anxiety, depression, loneliness, substance use shifts toward marijuana), and systemic barriers like short-term counseling models and long wait times. dr. gold also shares her take on ai as therapy, the generational stigma around meds, and how to manage your care independently when you're away from home. the conversation is honest about both individual challenges and what needs to change in college mental health systems.
quote: Talking is different than help seeking.
